sections.section_title: The Angelic Announcement of Babylon's Fall
sections.summary: The neutral reading presents an angel of overwhelming authority descending from heaven to announce Babylon's fall, declaring she has become a dwelling of demons and a prison of unclean spirits because all nations drank her wine; the section announces Babylon's fate rather than addressing the believer's standing.

sections.section_title: The Voice from Heaven -- Come Out of Her, My People
sections.summary: The neutral reading presents a divine voice commanding God's people to come out of Babylon so they will not participate in her sins and receive her plagues, followed by the decree of double repayment and sudden destruction.
sections.relevance: The command 'Come out of her, my people' (drawing on Jeremiah 51:45 and Isaiah 52:11) presupposes that God's own people (ho laos mou, the covenant designation) can be inside Babylon's system and must actively disengage. The neutral reading explicitly notes that 'the faithful are not in a separate, sealed-off community but are living within the imperial system' and that 'participation in sin leads to reception of plague.' The verb synkoinōnēsēte (to share in, participate with) indicates shared involvement, and the two purpose clauses -- 'so that you will not participate in her sins' and 'so that you will not receive of her plagues' -- establish a direct causal link between remaining in the system and sharing its judgment. The passage implies that God's people can share in Babylon's fate if they do not actively separate, which directly bears on the conditionality of their standing.
key_phrases: Come out of her, my people, so that you will not participate in her sins and receive of her plagues
for her sins have piled up as high as heaven

sections.section_title: The First Lament -- The Kings of the Earth
sections.summary: The neutral reading presents the kings of the earth weeping over Babylon's destruction, lamenting the sudden judgment of the great city; the section is a component of the funeral dirge rather than a statement about the believer's standing.

sections.section_title: The Second Lament -- The Merchants of the Earth
sections.summary: The neutral reading presents the merchants weeping because no one buys their cargoes anymore, listing twenty-eight luxury commodities culminating in 'bodies and souls of men'; the section is a commercial lament rather than a statement about the believer's standing.

The neutral reading presents the seafarers mourning Babylon's destruction, lamenting that the great city that enriched them was laid waste in one hour; the section is the final component of the funeral dirge rather than a statement about the believer's standing.

The neutral reading presents the command for heaven, saints, apostles, and prophets to rejoice because God has pronounced judgment against Babylon on their behalf; the section is a celebratory command rather than a statement about the believer's standing.

sections.section_title: The Millstone and the Silence of Babylon
sections.summary: The neutral reading presents the angel's millstone sign-act and the litany of silence (no more music, craft, grinding, light, or weddings), concluding with the indictment that in Babylon was found the blood of prophets, saints, and all who were slain on the earth; the section narrates Babylon's total and permanent destruction rather than addressing the believer's standing.
